notes: Splits out a bool-returning refresh so a caller with children takes its aggregate status, and emits when the run is settled. Clean and correct. The test uses a raw SQL update instead of existing helpers.

Cleanly refactors the refresh to report whether anything changed, so callers report a change only when there is one; the emit is tied to the settle branch, and the nested and force-cancel tests are solid.

Only the top caller skips cancellation while a descendant is cancelling. Nested callers still go through cancelOneJob and are written Cancelled, so the bug remains at depth >= 2, which the issue explicitly covers. It also always emits, and it edits a shared test helper.

Only skips cancelling the top caller when a descendant is cancelling, so intermediate nested callers are still force-written to cancelled and the issue's 'any nesting depth' case stays broken; the emitter is called on every cancel, and the shared createRunAttempt test helper is changed.

A caller with children now gets its status aggregated from them in cancelOneJob, so nested callers stay cancelling. Waiters are emitted when a run settles with no job update. Small risk: writing back an unchanged caller row through the affected-rows-checked UpdateRunJob path. Tests are thorough and actually unblock the waiter.

A minimal change sets a caller with children to its children's aggregate status; the tests are thorough, covering multi-child partial acks and actually running the emitter to show the waiting run starts.

Fixes the cancel path. It also changes RefreshReusableCallerStatus globally to walk ancestors and refresh the run on every no-op refresh, a broad hot-path behaviour change. The model test fabricates an artificial state and acks with SUCCESS.

Fixes the cancel path, but it also changes RefreshReusableCallerStatus so every unchanged-status child update walks up to refreshRunStatus, a hot-path change beyond the issue; its emit condition matches the reference, and its test relies on a contrived manual status overwrite.

A new helper refreshes callers with children from the aggregate, which handles nesting. The status check is redundant, and it emits whenever the run ends done, so emits are duplicated when jobs were updated. The service test verifies the waiter is selected.

Re-aggregates every caller that has children instead of cancelling it directly, which handles nested callers correctly; the emit fires whenever the run is done, even when jobs were updated, which is more often than needed.

Re-reads the caller and re-aggregates it from its children instead of forcing Cancelled, matching the reference's intent. The emit condition is tight. The nested model test covers the ack path; the service test only checks the emit.
Reloads the caller and re-aggregates it rather than cancelling it, with an emit condition close to the reference; it always reports the caller as updated, and its model test sits in task_test.go.
The caller-refresh fix works at any depth. It adds an unrequested de-duplication set to CancelJobs, emits whenever no job is updated, and has good depth-parameterised tests.
Correct caller re-aggregation inside cancelOneJob with good depth-1/2 tests, but it adds a dedupe in CancelJobs that the task did not require and always returns the reloaded caller as updated.

Keeps a caller cancelling only when its aggregate is exactly Cancelling and otherwise forces Cancelled rather than respecting the aggregate. It drops the task_id guard. The service test only asserts the emit.

The caller branch in cancelOneJob works at any depth, but it hard-codes Cancelled-or-Cancelling instead of using the full aggregate and always reports the caller as updated; it also emits on any cancel with no job updates.

A clean bool-returning refresh helper lets cancelOneJob derive caller status from its children, and a settled flag triggers the concurrency emit; it has a solid nested test, though the service test uses raw SQL.

A small refactor makes the refresh report whether it wrote anything, and callers with children are refreshed instead of cancelled; the settled-flag emit is clean, though the service test uses raw SQL and the import grouping is off.

Only skips cancelling the top-level caller, while nested callers among the descendants are still written Cancelled directly, so the nested case from the issue stays stuck (hidden test failed); it also emits on every cancel and changes a shared test helper.

It only holds the top-level caller in cancelling; nested callers in the descendant loop are still written Cancelled directly through cancelOneJob, so the issue's 'any nesting depth' case stays broken (consistent with 1/2 hidden), and it emits on every cancel and edits a shared test helper.

A caller with children takes the aggregate of its children inside cancelOneJob, so nested callers stay cancelling until the runner acknowledges, and a settled run emits for the concurrency check; the status/stopped assignment is a little convoluted, but the tests are thorough (nesting, attempts, partial acks, waiter actually unblocked).

A compact cancelOneJob change aggregates a caller's status from its children and clears stopped while non-final; the tests are the most thorough (two children acknowledged one at a time, a with/without-attempt matrix, and a check that the waiter actually transitions to Waiting).

Fixes the cancel path, but also changes RefreshReusableCallerStatus globally to walk ancestors and refresh the run on every no-op refresh, an invasive behavior and performance change well beyond the issue.

It works, but it globally changes RefreshReusableCallerStatus to walk up to the run whenever a caller's status is unchanged, an invasive cascade change with extra DB load; the test also oddly acknowledges with RESULT_SUCCESS to simulate already-stuck data.

The cancelOrRefreshReusableCaller approach for nested and top callers mirrors the reference well, but it emits whenever the run is done, even when job updates already emitted, causing redundant queue work.

A caller that has children (top-level or nested) is refreshed from them instead of being force-cancelled, which handles nesting correctly; the emit fires whenever the run is done, so it is redundant when jobs were already updated, and the tests cover two-level nesting plus cancel/force wake-up.

Refreshes a caller with children from a freshly read row instead of force-cancelling it, which is order-robust and close to the reference; it always reports the caller as updated even when unchanged, and the emit condition is tight and correct.

Callers with children are re-read fresh and refreshed rather than cancelled, closely matching the reference, and the emit condition is tight (only when the run newly becomes done); it slightly over-reports unchanged callers, and the nested test plus cancel/force service test are adequate.

A caller aggregates from its children via RefreshReusableCallerStatus and emits when no job was updated, but it adds an unrequested dedupe pass to CancelJobs, needed partly because its own change always returns the caller.

Callers with children are refreshed and re-read, which fixes nesting, but it adds an unrequested dedup set to CancelJobs and always reports callers as updated even when unchanged; the depth-parametrized test is solid.

Works for the reported case, but cancelCallerRow hardcodes Cancelled unless the aggregate is exactly Cancelling instead of adopting the children's aggregate, which is less principled; its service test only checks that an emit happened.

cancelOneJob keeps a caller cancelling while its children aggregate to cancelling and otherwise hard-codes Cancelled (dropping the task_id guard), which is slightly lossy versus a true aggregate; the nested test is good but the service test only checks that the emit fired.
